chunks: 34 - And with the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hafs al-A'sha; and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from a man from Banu Asad, all together, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, blessings of Allah be upon them both, who said:

I went out until I reached this wall, and I leaned against it, when suddenly a man wearing two white garments appeared. He looked in the direction of my face, then said: O Ali ibn al-Husayn, what is it that I see you sorrowful and grieving? Is it because of the worldly life? For the provision of Allah is present for the righteous and the sinful. He said: I said: It is not because of that I grieve, and indeed it is just as you say.

He said: Is it because of the Hereafter? For it is a truthful promise, judged by an Almighty King. I said: It is not because of that I grieve, and indeed it is just as you say. He said: Then what is your grief? I said: It is because of what we fear from the sedition of Ibn al-Zubayr.

He said: And he laughed, then said: O Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you ever seen anyone who feared Allah and He did not deliver him? He said: I said: No. He said: O Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you ever seen anyone who relied upon Allah and He did not suffice him? He said: I said: No. Then I looked and behold, there was no one before me.

key_terms.الْحَائِط: The wall; a garden wall where the Imam paused to rest
key_terms.تَوَكَّل: Tawakkul; reliance and trust in Allah
key_terms.فِتْنَة: Sedition, civil strife; here referring to the revolt of Ibn al-Zubayr
key_terms.مَلِكٌ قَاهِرٌ: An Almighty King; an attribute of Allah as the supreme judge
key_terms.وَعْدٌ صَادِقٌ: A truthful promise; referring to the promise of the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did the mysterious stranger teach Imam Zayn al-Abidin about trusting Allah during times of political turmoil?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) narrates a mysterious encounter near a wall during a time of political turmoil caused by Ibn al-Zubayr's revolt. A stranger in white garments approached him and, through a series of rhetorical questions, consoled him by affirming that neither worldly provisions nor the Hereafter should cause grief, since Allah provides for all and judges with absolute justice. When the Imam revealed his true worry - the political sedition of Ibn al-Zubayr - the stranger laughed and reminded him that whoever fears Allah is always delivered, and whoever relies upon Allah is always sufficed. The stranger then vanished, suggesting he may have been al-Khidr or an angelic figure sent to comfort the Imam.
